title: Bye-Bye, Bronze Letters: Workers Remove Trump's Name from the Kennedy Center
summary: Imagine waking up to see giant bronze letters being peeled off a famous building! That's what happened early Saturday at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C. Workers used scaffolding and tarps to remove President Donald Trump's name from the front of the building. The name had been added just six months ago, but a judge ruled it had to come down. Why? Because only Congress—not the president—can rename the Kennedy Center. The government tried to stop the removal, arguing that Trump's name helped bring in money for repairs. But a higher court said no. So, in the middle of the night, while rain and thunderstorms soaked the city, workers got the job done. Some people cheered, while others shouted "Cowards!" because the work was hidden behind tarps. One onlooker, Krystal Brewer, said removing the name was about "enforcing accountability" and not letting anyone defy the courts just because they're powerful. Another person, Mary Foltz, called the hidden removal a "metaphor" for the Trump administration. The whole drama started when Trump took over the Kennedy Center's board and added his name. Now, the building is back to being just the Kennedy Center—for now.
why_it_matters: This story shows that in a democracy, even the most powerful people have to follow rules set by courts and lawmakers, which protects everyone's rights.

background_read: The Kennedy Center is named after President John F. Kennedy, who led the United States in the early 1960s and was tragically shot in 1963.
In the U.S., only Congress has the power to name federal buildings; the president cannot do it alone, even if he or she appoints the people who run the building.
Donald Trump added his name to the Kennedy Center after becoming president again in 2025, but a court decided that was against the law and ordered the letters taken off.
Article_Structure: WHO: Workers using scaffolding and tarps, a judge, and former President Donald Trump.
WHAT: Giant bronze letters spelling Trump's name were peeled off the Kennedy Center overnight after a court ruling.
WHERE: At the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., the capital of the United States.
WHY: Because a judge said only Congress, not the president, can rename the building, so adding the name was illegal.

perspectives.description: People who wanted the name gone cheered, saying it was a victory for the rule of law and that no one, not even a president, can ignore a court's order.
Supporters of Trump felt the removal was done sneakily, hidden behind tarps, and they shouted 'Cowards!' because they thought the workers should have done it openly.
Some, like Mary Foltz, thought the whole secretive removal was like a metaphor for how that administration sometimes worked — hiding things instead of being open.
